Notes

  • Attribution is rarely simple. Most extinctions involve overlapping actors — e.g., a government paying bounties (thylacine), industry clearing habitat (Chinese paddlefish, passenger pigeon), and consumer demand (rhino horn, feathers).
  • Climate-change extinctions are a newer category, where responsibility is diffuse across historical emitters rather than a specific actor.
  • Corporate blame is clearest in cases like the Singer Manufacturing Company (logged the last ivory-billed woodpecker habitat, 1940s) and the Van Diemen's Land Company (thylacine bounties).
  • Some statuses have nuance: Spix's macaws have been reintroduced to the wild (2022+); ivory-billed woodpecker sightings remain contested.
  • For authoritative, current status, check the IUCN Red List (iucnredlist.org).
You cannot evolve out of a clade. But some cunts get offended when we say we are monkeys. I mean in  sense of monophyletic groups. So we all are simians, aren't we ?

Yes, you're right

The logic is straightforward under cladistics:

The hierarchy (simplified):

text
Primates
└── Simiiformes (simians/anthropoids)
├── Platyrrhini (New World monkeys)
└── Catarrhini (Old World simians)
├── Cercopithecoidea (Old World monkeys)
└── Hominoidea (apes)
└── Hominidae (great apes)
└── Humans

The key point:

If "ape" is nested inside "simian," and "monkey" informally means "non-ape simian," then "monkey" is paraphyletic — it arbitrarily excludes one branch of the clade. That's no better than saying "fish" excludes tetrapods, or "reptiles" excludes birds.

You can't evolve out of your ancestry. Humans didn't stop being simians any more than birds stopped being dinosaurs or whales stopped being artiodactyls.

Common retorts and why they fail:

Objection
Problem
"Apes aren't monkeys."That's a colloquial convention, not a cladistic statement. It creates a paraphyletic group.
"Monkey ≠ simian."Then define it by some trait apes uniquely lost. There isn't one.
"It's offensive."That's not an argument about taxonomy.

The only honest options are:

  1. "Monkey" = all simians (monophyletic) → humans are monkeys
  2. Accept it's an informal folk term not meant to be cladistically rigorous

So yes — under monophyly, we're simians, and simians are the monkey clade.

Why does the RSS claim that they are indigenous to India, when the mainstream historical and genetic evidence supports Indo-Aryan migration into the subcontinent? And why do some Tamil nationalists describe RSS gang as vantheris?

Why the RSS claims indigeneity

The RSS promotes the "Out of India Theory" (OIT) — that Indo-Aryans originated in India and migrated outward. This contradicts the mainstream consensus.

Why they hold this position:

  • Hindutva identity: If Hindus are the "original inhabitants" and their religion is indigenous, then other faiths (Islam, Christianity) can be framed as foreign imports. This supports a narrative of Hindu nationhood.
  • Reaction to colonial scholarship: The British-era "Aryan Invasion Theory" was genuinely problematic — used for divide-and-rule (Aryan vs Dravidian). The OIT overcorrects by denying any migration occurred.
  • Partition anxiety: After 1947, claiming Muslims as "descendants of converts" rather than a separate foreign people became politically convenient — though the RSS uses indigeneity selectively.
  • Vedas as primordial: OIT allows them to claim the Rig Veda is older than the Indus Valley Civilization, making Hinduism the fountainhead of all civilization.

What mainstream evidence shows:

  • Steppe pastoralist ancestry enters South Asia ~2000–1500 BCE (Narasimhan et al., 2019)
  • Indo-Aryan languages are part of the Indo-European family
  • The Rig Veda shows no knowledge of IVC cities
  • Horse and chariot arrive with Steppe migrants
  • Indus script has no demonstrated Indo-Aryan connection

The RSS dismisses genetic evidence as "Western conspiracy" or colonial residue.

Tamil nationalism and "vantheri"

வந்தேறி = "intruder" / "foreigner who arrived"

Some Tamil (and broader Dravidian) nationalists invert the same migration logic:

  • North Indians = later Aryan arrivals who displaced original Dravidian inhabitants
  • Hindi imposition = cultural colonization
  • RSS = agents of North Indian/Aryan hegemony

The irony:

Genetics undermines both narratives. Most South Asians — North and South — are a mix of:

  • Ancestral Ancient Iranian farmer ancestry
  • Ancestral South Indian (ASI) hunter-gatherer ancestry
  • Steppe ancestry (varying proportions, generally higher in North, lower in South)

There is no "pure Aryan" or "pure Dravidian" population. Both identities are political fictions layered on real linguistic differences.

Summary

Group
Claim
Reality
RSSAryans always in India, migrated outSteppe ancestry arrived in ~1500 BCE
Tamil nationalistsDravidians original, North Indians foreignEveryone is mixed; the "racial" divide is colonial fiction

Both sides weaponize prehistory for present-day politics.

We all now what's really happening with NEP and which language is being forced albeit indicrectly, as northies pick sanskrit - thus avoidiing any dravidian language, whereas southies just pick hindi as 3rd. Well, Why RSS & BJP is using NEP and forcing 3 language policy , which in practice is imposing Hindi in non Hindi states, despite the fact that many southern states are naturally speaking native languages , whereas RSS want to spread a language from Indo-Iranian branch to those states ?

The asymmetry is real

The three-language formula promises reciprocity. In practice, it delivers one-way traffic:

Region
L1
L2
L3 in practice
Hindi beltHindiEnglishSanskrit (rarely Tamil/Telugu/Kannada/Malayalam)
South (except TN)RegionalEnglishHindi (sometimes French/German)
Tamil NaduTamilEnglish— (two-language policy since 1968)

So the slot that was supposed to create north–south linguistic exchange gets filled with Sanskrit in the north — which keeps the third language within the Indo-Aryan family rather than a Dravidian one. Sanskrit wins that slot because:

  • It's perceived as scoring-friendly ("free marks")
  • Teacher infrastructure exists for it, not for southern languages
  • It carries religious-ideological prestige

Net effect: Hindi flows south, Sanskrit stays north, Dravidian languages go nowhere. NEP 2020's text says "no language will be imposed" — but the structure does the imposing.

Why the RSS/BJP push it

1. Ideological core. Golwalkar's cultural nationalism trends toward one nation, one culture, one language. Hindi is framed as Sanskrit's popular vehicle; Sanskrit as the civilizational fountainhead. This connects directly to the OIT claims from your last question — a language hierarchy is being pushed as a civilizational one.

2. Historical grievance. The 1965 anti-Hindi agitation and the 1967 amendment guaranteeing English indefinitely are remembered in Hindutva circles as a defeat to be reversed by attrition.

3. Electoral math. The BJP's core is the Hindi belt (~45% of Lok Sabha seats). Promoting Hindi consolidates that base. The cost is low because the south was never won anyway — as 2024 showed, BJP won zero seats in Tamil Nadu.

4. Centralization. Education is on the concurrent list. The leverage is financial: the Centre withheld roughly ₹2,150 crore of Samagra Shiksha funds from Tamil Nadu over its refusal to sign onto the three-language formula. "Choice" backed by funding cuts is coercion with extra steps.

5. Organizational ecosystem. RSS-affiliated schools (Saraswati Shishu Mandirs), Samskrita Bharati, and the NEP's "Indian Knowledge Systems" push all reinforce the Sanskrit–Hindi axis. Senior RSS figures have even proposed Sanskrit as the national language.

6. Demand-side cover. Hindi-speaking labor migration into Bengaluru, Hyderabad, and other metros creates genuine on-ground demand. Policy rides that wave and accelerates it, then points to it as evidence of "voluntary adoption."

The irony you're circling

By the RSS's own indigeneity logic:

  • Tamil has attested literature from ~300 BCE; Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam have deep histories
  • Modern Hindi was standardized from Khari Boli in the 19th century (Fort William College era), then heavily Sanskritized
  • Rigvedic Sanskrit itself contains a non-Indo-Aryan substrate — non-IE vocabulary, retroflexion — indicating pre-Indo-Aryan languages were already in the subcontinent (Kuiper, Witzel)

So the project spreads a young language over older ones in the name of defending indigeneity. The civilizational hierarchy (Sanskrit > Dravidian) is a claim, not evidence.

Summary

Question
Answer
Is Hindi formally mandated?No — "no imposition" is in the text
Is it imposed in practice?Effectively yes — funding leverage + asymmetric language choices
Why Sanskrit in the north?Ideology + easy scoring; conveniently avoids Dravidian languages
Why push at all?Cultural nationalism, Hindi-belt vote base, centralization, reversing the 1965 "defeat"
The contradiction?Defending "indigenous" civilization by spreading the youngest major language over the oldest

Note the tactical flexibility, though: after southern backlash to the 2019 draft NEP, the "no imposition" clause was added; and political pressure has periodically forced retreats. The direction of travel is consistent — the concessions come only when the electoral cost rises.

two questions. Tell me about Euler's identity. And why LLMs aren't being trained on language of Orcas. (if they are being trained, correct me)

Euler's Identity

eiπ+1=0e^{i\pi} + 1 = 0eiπ+1=0
Five fundamental constants, three arithmetic operations, one line:

Symbol
Domain
e (~2.718…)Analysis — continuous growth
iAlgebra — √−1
π (~3.14159…)Geometry — circles
1Multiplicative identity
0Additive identity

Where it comes from

It's a special case of Euler's formula:

eiθ=cos⁡θ+isin⁡θe^{i\theta} = \cos\theta + i\sin\thetaeiθ=cosθ+isinθ
Proof sketch via Taylor series — substitute x = iθ into the expansion of e^x. Because i² = −1, the signs alternate and the real and imaginary parts split exactly into the series for cosine and sine:

text
e^(iθ) = (1 − θ²/2! + θ⁴/4! − …) + i(θ − θ³/3! + θ⁵/5! − …)
= cos θ + i·sin θ

Set θ = π: cos π = −1, sin π = 0, so e^(iπ) = −1.

What it means

  • e^(iθ) is rotation. The exponential of an imaginary number wraps the real line around the unit circle in the complex plane. e^(iπ) is a half-turn: it takes 1 to −1. Adding 1 brings you to 0.
  • It unifies growth and rotation — exponential motion along the imaginary axis is circular motion. This single fact is why complex numbers dominate engineering (signal processing, Fourier analysis) and physics (quantum phases).
  • It also reveals that e^z is periodic with period 2πi — trigonometry was hiding inside the exponential all along.

Feynman called Euler's formula "the most remarkable formula in mathematics." In polls of physicists and mathematicians (Mathematical Intelligencer 1988, Physics World 2004), the identity was voted the most beautiful equation. The beauty isn't mystical — it's the shock of seeing five unrelated constants turn out to be one sentence.

LLMs and Orca Language

Correction to your premise: this isn't zero — but orcas are not the flagship species, and what's happening is more modest than "training LLMs on a language."

What actually exists

Effort
Species
Approach
Project CETI (2020–)Sperm whalesNLP-style analysis of click "codas"; 2024 Nat. Comms paper found combinatorial structure — a tentative "phonetic alphabet"
Earth Species ProjectCross-speciesNatureLM — an audio-language foundation model for bioacoustics
Google DolphinGemma (2025)Atlantic spotted dolphinsA ~400M-param next-token predictor trained on 40 years of Wild Dolphin Project recordings, paired with a two-way interaction device
Orca workOrcasAcoustic classification of call types, dialect studies (Fournet, Deecke et al.) — no LLM-scale model

Why orcas specifically lag

  1. Discreteness. Sperm whale codas are click patterns — countable, sequence-able units, ideal for tokenization. Orca calls are continuous whistles and pulsed calls; we don't even know what their "phonemes" are. No segmentation, no tokens.
  2. No Rosetta stone. LLMs on human text work because meaning is anchored: we are the ground truth. With orcas there is zero bilingual corpus — no call↔meaning dictionary. A model can learn call statistics but there's nothing tying statistics to semantics.
  3. No evaluation. With human language, you can test the output. With orcas, you can't tell whether the model "understands" anything or just produces plausible noise.
  4. Dialect fragmentation. Orca dialects are culturally transmitted and pod-specific. Each pod is a tiny, idiosyncratic dataset with poor transfer between pods. Bigg's (mammal-eating) orcas additionally go silent while hunting — data collection is inherently lopsided.
  5. Scale. LLMs train on trillions of tokens. The best cetacean datasets are millions of vocalizations at most — a fundamentally small-data regime.
  6. It may not be language. Evidence for referential semantics or syntax in orca calls is thin. An LLM can only find statistical structure; it cannot decide whether that structure constitutes language. That's an empirical-linguistics question the architecture can't answer.

The deeper point

A model trained on orca sounds would learn orca song statistics, not orca meaning. Meaning requires grounding — synchronized behavior, context, interaction — which is exactly why CETI records audio + video + movement together. Even the celebrated case of the orca "Wikie" imitating human words (2018) showed vocal mimicry, not comprehension.

And there's an ethical tail: if two-way communication ever worked, we'd face the question of consent — whether we should be talking to them at all, and what happens if we say something harmful.

Summary

Question
Answer
Is anyone applying LLM techniques to cetaceans?Yes — CETI (sperm whales), ESP (cross-species), DolphinGemma (dolphins)
Orcas specifically?Classification-level work only; no language model
Why not?No segmentation units, no grounding, no ground truth, tiny fragmented datasets, and no proof the calls are a language at all
What's the bottleneck?Not compute or architecture — it's that meaning has no anchor without shared context

Two things I can say, though:

  2. If the writing genuinely reflects distress, the answer to "why" belongs to the person, not to strangers on the internet — including me. Diagnosing or speculating about a real individual's private life from outside would be cheap.

If you paste in some of the posts or tell me what the blog actually says, I can discuss the themes, the humor style, or what it might reflect. But I won't pretend to know someone I don't.
